There are no restrictions on using the money in or outside India.

summary: The ITR-2 asks individuals to choose one residential status: Resident, Resident but not Ordinarily resident (RNOR), or Non-resident. If you are a resident or RNOR, you also tick the basis for your claim. A non-resident gives the country of residence and tax identification number. These instructions are for assessment year 2020-21 and do not explain how the status itself is decided.

summary: Under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, a resident individual can remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year (April to March) for permitted current or capital account transactions, or both. That covers things like gifts, supporting close relatives, buying shares, funds or property abroad, and repaying a loan taken abroad while a non-resident. A PAN is mandatory. This circular is from 1 July 2015, so check the current limit with your bank.

findings.statement: Authorised dealers may freely allow remittances by resident individuals up to USD 250,000 per financial year for permitted current or capital account transactions, or both.

citations.quote: Authorised Dealers may freely allow remittances by resident individuals up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year (April -March) for any permitted current or capital account transactions or a combination of both

findings.statement: The scheme is available to all resident individuals, including minors.

citations.quote: The Scheme is available to all resident individuals including minors

findings.statement: Residents can acquire and hold shares, debt instruments or any other asset, including immovable property, outside India without prior RBI approval.

citations.quote: Resident individuals are free to acquire and hold shares or debt instruments or any other asset including immovable property outside India without prior approval of the Reserve Bank

findings.statement: A person who took a loan abroad as a non-resident can repay it on returning to India under the scheme.

citations.quote: An individual who has availed of a loan abroad while as a non -resident can repay the same on return to India under the Scheme as a resident

findings.statement: Gifts and supporting close relatives abroad are covered by the same limit.

citations.quote: A resident individual can remit up-to USD 250,000 per financial year towards maintenance of close relatives

findings.statement: A PAN is mandatory to remit under the scheme, and it is not available for capital account remittances to countries named by the Financial Action Task Force.

citations.quote: It is mandatory to have PAN number to make remittances under the Scheme
The Scheme is not available for capital account remittances to countries identified by Financial Action Task Force

roadmap.step: Make sure you have a PAN before you remit under the scheme.

roadmap.step: Ask your bank for the current limit and forms before sending money abroad, because this circular dates from 2015.

missing_information.why_it_matters: The scheme is for resident individuals.

confidence_reason: The RBI Master Circular is dated 1 July 2015. The scheme's limit and conditions may have been updated since, so confirm the current ones with your bank.
